evidence.title: Raman Spectroscopy of Diesel and Gasoline Engine-Out Soot Using Different Laser Power
evidence.abstract: We studied engine-out soot samples collected from a heavy-duty direct-injection diesel engine and a port-fuel injection gasoline spark-ignition engine. The two types of soot samples were characterized using Raman spectroscopy with different laser power. A Matlab program using least-square-method with trust-region-reflective algorithm was developed for curve fitting. We used a DOE (design of experiments) method to avoid local convergence. This method was used for two-band fitting and three-band fitting. The fitting results were used to determine the intensity ratio of D and G Raman bands. We find that high laser power may cause oxidation of soot samples, which gives higher D/G intensity ratio. Diesel soot has consistently higher amorphous/graphitic carbon ratio and thus higher oxidation reactivity, in comparison to gasoline soot, which is revealed by the higher D/G intensity ratio in Raman spectra measured under the same laser power.

evidence.title: Towards Long-endurance Flight: Design and Implementation of a Variable-pitch Gasoline-engine Quadrotor
evidence.abstract: Majority of today's fixed-pitch, electric-power quadrotors have short flight endurance ($<$ 1 hour) which greatly limits their applications. This paper presents a design methodology for the construction of a long-endurance quadrotor using variable-pitch rotors and a gasoline-engine. The methodology consists of three aspects. Firstly, the rotor blades and gasoline engine are selected as a pair, so that sufficient lift can be comfortably provided by the engine. Secondly, drivetrain and airframe are designed. Major challenges include airframe vibration minimization and power transmission from one engine to four rotors while keeping alternate rotors contra-rotating. Lastly, a PD controller is tuned to facilitate preliminary flight tests. The methodology has been verified by the construction and successful flight of our gasoline quadrotor prototype, which is designed to have a flight time of 2 to 3 hours and a maximum take-off weight of 10 kg.

evidence.title: Variable length connecting rod
evidence.abstract: A variable length connecting rod for an engine comprises a floating bush slidably mounted within a body of the connecting rod with chambers on opposing sides of the bush. Hydraulic fluid is transferred between the chambers via at least one channel to move the bush and shorten or lengthen the connecting rod. Embodiments of the connecting rod comprise a lever connected to a variable one way valve which controls the direction of flow of the hydraulic fluid between the chambers. Movement of the hydraulic fluid between the chambers is driven by pressure differentials resulting from the movement of the connecting rod

mechanism_map.mechanism: Raman spectroscopy characterization of soot to determine amorphous/graphitic carbon ratio and oxidation reactivity
mechanism_map.intervention: Implement in-line Raman spectroscopy at the factory to analyze combustion byproducts from prototype engines, using the D/G intensity ratio to verify fuel-air mixture homogeneity and combustion completeness, thereby identifying manufacturing variances in fuel injectors or cylinder geometry that lead to localized overheating and connecting rod bearing failure.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Detection and correction of specific manufacturing defects causing incomplete combustion and excessive thermal load before mass production, resolving the root cause rather than masking symptoms with ECU updates.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Compare D/G intensity ratios from Raman spectra of soot samples collected from engines with known good bearings versus engines with documented bearing failures; if the ratios show no statistically significant difference correlating to the defect, the mechanism is falsified.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: Diesel soot has consistently higher amorphous/graphitic carbon ratio

custody_records.raw_content: We studied engine-out soot samples collected from a heavy-duty direct-injection diesel engine and a port-fuel injection gasoline spark-ignition engine. The two types of soot samples were characterized using Raman spectroscopy with different laser power. A Matlab program using least-square-method with trust-region-reflective algorithm was developed for curve fitting. We used a DOE (design of experiments) method to avoid local convergence. This method was used for two-band fitting and three-band fitting. The fitting results were used to determine the intensity ratio of D and G Raman bands. We find that high laser power may cause oxidation of soot samples, which gives higher D/G intensity ratio. Diesel soot has consistently higher amorphous/graphitic carbon ratio and thus higher oxidation reactivity, in comparison to gasoline soot, which is revealed by the higher D/G intensity ratio in Raman spectra measured under the same laser power.

custody_records.raw_content: Majority of today's fixed-pitch, electric-power quadrotors have short flight endurance ($<$ 1 hour) which greatly limits their applications. This paper presents a design methodology for the construction of a long-endurance quadrotor using variable-pitch rotors and a gasoline-engine. The methodology consists of three aspects. Firstly, the rotor blades and gasoline engine are selected as a pair, so that sufficient lift can be comfortably provided by the engine. Secondly, drivetrain and airframe are designed. Major challenges include airframe vibration minimization and power transmission from one engine to four rotors while keeping alternate rotors contra-rotating. Lastly, a PD controller is tuned to facilitate preliminary flight tests. The methodology has been verified by the construction and successful flight of our gasoline quadrotor prototype, which is designed to have a flight time of 2 to 3 hours and a maximum take-off weight of 10 kg.

custody_records.raw_content: A variable length connecting rod for an engine comprises a floating bush slidably mounted within a body of the connecting rod with chambers on opposing sides of the bush. Hydraulic fluid is transferred between the chambers via at least one channel to move the bush and shorten or lengthen the connecting rod. Embodiments of the connecting rod comprise a lever connected to a variable one way valve which controls the direction of flow of the hydraulic fluid between the chambers. Movement of the hydraulic fluid between the chambers is driven by pressure differentials resulting from the movement of the connecting rod
